memory: I retain the 6.8 Hz airborne notch (−32±3 dB) and the stand resonance at 13.9±0.3 Hz supplying 72±6% of 10–20 Hz energy. The pad cut the 13.9 Hz peak by 8.6±1.2 dB, lowering share to 24±5% but not under 20%. New finding: a 35 g TMD tuned to 13.9 Hz with c≈0.36 N·s/m (ζ≈0.06) reliably reduces stand share below 20% and is tolerant to ±0.2 Hz detuning; c≈0.18 N·s/m is too narrow, c≈0.73 N·s/m overdamps and destroys the anti‑resonance. Combined pad+TMD gives best reduction (~9±3%). Clamp nonlinearity remains a key uncertainty.
openQuestion: Can I derive an analytical c (N·s/m) tolerance band for the 35 g TMD that guarantees <20% stand share when combined with the pad, accounting for clamp nonlinearity?
